items.title: 9.1.3 How Does Design Thinking Apply to Business Solutions?

source_refs.note: Topic 9.1.3 with the class activity (PDF 209, printed 206). Long question 1 is answered; the activity outputs and the grocery example are illustrative, flagged.

blocks.text: Design thinking helps companies create products and services that people actually want. A company might use it to build an app that makes ordering food online easier, focusing on the user's experience and testing different ideas until the app is both easy to use and successful.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: apply design thinking to students who cannot find time for homework because of after-school activities. What might each step produce?
blocks.explanation: Empathize: interviews show students feel rushed and tired. Define: 'students need a way to fit homework around activities'. Ideate: a shared planner, a homework hour at college, fewer weekday activities. Prototype: a weekly timetable template. Test: students try it for a week and suggest changes, which are built into the next version.

blocks.prompt: Discuss the importance of design thinking in developing business solutions, with examples (long question 1).
blocks.explanation: Design thinking reduces the risk of building something nobody wants, because it starts from users' real needs and tests ideas cheaply with prototypes before spending heavily. It encourages many ideas, so solutions are more creative, and its repeated testing improves products step by step. Examples: a food-ordering app refined through user tests; a school bag designed from students' complaints; a grocery store redesigning its delivery service after asking customers what frustrates them.

items: Design thinking makes business solutions user-centred and tested (food-ordering app).
